# SB-1014 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated from abrasive blasting operations in proximity to machining and part handling areas presents an inhalation, respiratory sensitization, and combustible dust ignition hazard. Dust accumulation on machine enclosures, electrical cabinets, and tooling increases the risk of equipment malfunction and fire. Fine particulate can enter cutting fluid sumps and coolant systems, degrade filtration, and compromise part tolerances through contamination. Personnel performing setup, maintenance, and part loading are at highest exposure risk without appropriate controls.

Affected equipment
Primary affected unit: EQ-P1-L3-CN03 (Machining CNC turning center #3). Adjacent stations on line P1-L3 that receive blasted parts for subsequent operations are also impacted. Note: The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m.

Required controls
- Engineering controls: Maintain local exhaust ventilation and blasting enclosure integrity to prevent dust migration into machining areas. Inspect blast enclosure seals and exhaust filters per SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03. Ensure machining enclosures remain closed during blasting operations.
- Administrative controls: Coordinate blasting schedules with machining to allow time for dust settling and cleaning. Update procedure steps in SOP-P1-L3-05 to include verification of part cleanliness prior to mounting. Train operators on dust recognition and reporting requirements.
- Housekeeping and PPE: Implement daily cleaning of machine exteriors, coolant sumps, and work surfaces with methods that minimize airborne re-entrainment (wet wiping or HEPA-filtered vacuum). Require respiratory protection and eye protection when entering areas during or immediately after blasting until air monitoring confirms acceptable levels.
- Mechanical safeguards: Before reusing tooling or re-clamping parts, visually inspect mating surfaces and fasteners for dust; clean as necessary. Follow documented torque specification when reassembling chuck components.

Effective date
Effective upon issuance. Consult SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-03, and SOP-P1-L3-05 for detailed procedures and verification checklists.
